panels.description: Wide, full page width. A weary Travancore column in monsoon-wet paddy, turning north. Bullocks and men haul cannon through ankle-deep mud along a narrow village bund. Mid-column, Nagoji on Kayal, his bay mare with a coat the ochre red-brown of earth after rain. Nagoji in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble. Mud to the mare's knees. Grey sky.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In 1741, by the time we closed our ring around Colachel, we were already tired from another war.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The same guns had faced Chanda Sahib's lines in the south.

panels.description: Flashback. Tight, a narrow strip; the hands sit in the right two-thirds. A contract on a table, its lines indistinct marks with no legible lettering. A Dutch hand in a blue cuff holds the paper flat. A mature woman's hand, lightly lined, with gold bangles, presses a seal into red wax. We do not see her face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Two years before Colachel, the company had decided to stop being a guest at our table.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They took up the grievance of the Elayadathu line at Kottarakkara, a princess Varma had pushed aside, and promised her Dutch support for pepper signed cheap under her seal.

panels.description: Flashback. The Colachel shore. Burned fishermen's huts, blackened palm thatch, upturned boats. Far out on the grey water, three Dutch ships at anchor, plain tricolours with no monogram, low smoke drifting from their gun ports.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The November before Colachel, they tested this coast and left a warning written in salt and ash.

panels.description: Flashback. A village street near Kottar. Dutch East India Company soldiers in blue coats sit at ease on a verandah, muskets stacked, one man eating from a banana leaf. A plain tricolour hangs from the eave, no lettering. Villagers watch from doorways, silent.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Desinganadu, Kochi, Purakkad, Thekkumkur, each nursing its own wounds, were quick to stand under that foreign umbrella.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a few months, Padmanabhapuram seemed already within their reach.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Back to full colour. Marthanda Varma (varma-v1 face; cream-and-gold cloth, cream turban, gold necklaces) on horseback at the head of his staff, mud on his legs, reining north. Tired eyes, set jaw. Rain beginning.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Dutch had not come when Travancore was fresh and waiting.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They were striking a man who had only just pushed one invader back, and had not yet found his footing again.

panels.description: Wide, high angle over the siege. Our trench lines curve around the Dutch beachhead in a closing ring of earthworks, revetted with palm trunks and woven mats. Batteries puff white smoke. Inside, a shrinking blue and grey mass of men pressed against the sea. Heat haze and salt spray.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The war became a weight, not a collision.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: There was no grand charge, no thunder of hooves as I had imagined in restless sleep. Only the slow, grinding work of earth and patience.

panels.description: At a trench parapet. Dhanaji (stockier and a little shorter than Nagoji, short black beard, white turban, indigo-dyed tunic, no sash, talwar at his hip) wipes sweat from his eyes. Nagoji beside him in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble. Beyond, a fresh plume of smoke rises from the Dutch camp.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: They are stubborn.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: Most men would have swum for the ships by now.

panels.description: Nagoji, eyes on the enemy camp, calm.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They are waiting for help that is not coming.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And they are afraid to admit the great Company has been trapped by a king they thought was a petty chieftain.

panels.description: Inland scrub and low palms. Ponnan (bare-headed, curly hair uncovered, broad-shouldered Maravar, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, white mundu hitched above bare knees, short jacket) leads light Maravar horse weaving through the brush. A Dutch forager in a faded blue coat, bareheaded, water skins slung over his shoulder, has been ridden down; he drops the skins and raises his hands before a lowered lance.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My riders did not charge squares. We became the gaolers of the perimeter.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Ponnan's Maravar closed gaps my Deccan eyes would have missed.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Night. Nagoji alone at the water's edge, far from the batteries, a small figure in the rust-red turban against a black, heaving sea. Monsoon cloud over the moon. Nothing visible on the water.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But this war had two fronts: the land where we stood, and the sea where the fishermen ruled.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: No sane man sailed these waters in the dark during the rains.

panels.description: Wide. The black surf, and on it, shadows. Low, narrow boats blackened with soot slip through the waves. Mukkuvar men, bodies oiled and glistening, paddle almost without a splash.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But it was alive.

panels.description: A group of them dragging a craft up the sand, grinning, teeth white in the gloom. Nagoji walking toward them in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Good fishing?

panels.description: Antony, a Mukkuvar headman: lean and tall, oiled and bare-chested, loincloth only, rope scars across his forearms and a pale nick through one eyebrow, a small wooden cross on a cord at his neck. No scar on his cheek or jaw. He spits a stream of betel juice into the sand.

copy.speaker: ANTONY
copy.text: Very good, Ayya. We found a supply boat coming in from a ship further out.

copy.speaker: ANTONY
copy.text: It has a hole in its hull now. The rice is for the fish.

panels.description: Two-shot. Nagoji asking; Antony shrugs and gestures toward the dark water.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And the crew?

copy.speaker: ANTONY
copy.text: Some swam. The sea is hungry tonight.

copy.speaker: ANTONY
copy.text: They think big ships make them masters. But big ships must anchor. And anchors act like tethers for goats.

panels.description: Full width, bottom, at the waterline far offshore. The towering black hull of a Dutch ship, no flag lettering or monogram. Its anchor cable runs down into the sea, and on it, half submerged, a dark swimmer with a blade in his teeth and both hands on the rope.

copy.speaker: ANTONY (off)
copy.text: We swim out, we cut, we drill.

copy.speaker: ANTONY (off)
copy.text: They are fighting the ocean, and the ocean is on our side.

panels.description: Wide, dusk. Nair sappers (forward-tied topknots, bare chests, short white mundus) push our trench line closer to the stockade, earth flying from their spades. Inset in the upper corner: Varma at Tiruvattar (varma-v1 face; attach the Varma sheet), bare-headed and bare-chested in a white cloth, barefoot on the stone steps of the Adi Kesava temple, praying as a devotee. Ghee lamps behind him, river water over black stone. Not the temple-priest face; if a priest tends the lamps, he is a separate, smaller figure behind. Anchor the first caption over the inset and leave the sappers open.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In late May, when the air began to taste of rain, Varma rode north to Tiruvattar and begged Adi Kesava Swami for success.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He came back without ceremony.

panels.description: The Dutch camp seen over our parapet. Mud ramparts sagging under their own guns, one cannon tilted into slumped earth. Sick men lying under torn canvas. Empty barrels stacked by a wall. Among the sick, small in frame, Lieutenant Rijtel: a short, dark-haired Dutch officer in a blue coat with an officer's sash.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: At sea, Ibrahim's divers and boatmen bled their supplies and nerves.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Hackert, the commander they had trusted, had gone north with fresh troops. Lieutenant Rijtel was left to hold this shrinking patch of sand.

panels.description: Distant, through heat shimmer. A tall, pale-haired figure in a Dutch blue coat paces the Dutch perimeter, pushing men into a gap, pointing. Too far to see a face, only the height and pale hair catching the light. A thin, ragged volley puffs from the wall.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Yet they held.

panels.description: Evening, under a camp awning. Ramayyan (older, thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, bare-headed, plain white cloth, no jewellery) stands over a spread of palm-leaf casualty reports, a leaf bundle in his hand; the leaves carry indistinct marks, no legible writing. Varma (varma-v1 face; cream-and-gold cloth, cream turban, gold necklaces) sits on a camp stool, sharpening a small knife on a whetstone across his knee, eyes on the distant Dutch fires. Nagoji stands at the edge of the lamplight in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They are stubborn. Good officers, wasted on a merchant's war.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They think they serve their nation.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Ramayyan, close, lit from below by the lamp. Behind him, Varma's hand and the knife have gone still on the whetstone.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They serve a company.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Merchants who will check the cost of their rescue against the price of pepper, and decide they are too expensive.

panels.description: Wide. Sun blazing on wet sand, the air shimmering. At our main battery nearest the beach, gunners slump in the heat, one asleep against a wheel. The Dutch stockade beyond, quiet.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The 10th of August. The end, when it came, arrived on a wind from the sea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The siege stank of unburied waste and rotting fish and burnt powder.

panels.description: Insert, memory. A palm leaf on a floor, a hand with a stick of charcoal (Karl August's: pale, sickly yellow cast, rough cotton cuff). The coastline, a small square, one corner shaded.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of Karl August's charcoal on Ramayyan's leaf, where powder and rice lay too close together.

panels.description: Nagoji on Kayal in the commander look (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble), reining up beside a Nair captain at the battery: young, muscular, forward-tied topknot, bare chest, short white mundu, round shield slung on his back, no turban.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Wake them up.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If the Dutch think we are sleeping, they might try a sortie.

panels.description: The gun crew at work: one sponges the bore, one rams the charge home, a third squints along the barrel against the glare, hand on the elevation wedge. The barrel points at the heart of the Dutch fort.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: By habit, toward where Ramayyan had quietly told them the enemy kept its teeth.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The gun fires. A puff of white smoke, the barrel kicking back. Nagoji watching, still.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I do not believe in luck. I believe in preparation meeting opportunity.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But sometimes, war throws dice.

panels.description: Wide and bright. The ball, a dark speck against a hard blue sky, arcing over the Dutch outer wall and a row of tents where the sick lie. Leave the upper corner of sky for the 6.2 inset.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It dropped with the precision of a hawk.

panels.description: Inset over the sky of 6.1, tight. The moment after impact, at the heart of the Dutch camp: a small stone church used as a storehouse, a fresh ragged hole in its roof, dust sifting down onto the powder barrels stacked in its doorway beside sacks of rice. A single Dutch soldier in a blue coat stares up at the hole.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a heartbeat, nothing happened.

panels.description: Large, about 45% of the page. Blinding glare at the centre of the blast, bleaching toward the edges; the foreground figures stay legible. A pillar of flame and boiling black smoke stands over the Dutch camp, debris spinning in its heart. In the foreground our forward trench, men flung flat by the blast. Kayal rearing, Nagoji hauling on the reins, the loose end of his red sash whipping back. Nagoji in the commander look: compact rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, boots; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud.

Dhanaji (white turban, indigo-dyed tunic, short black beard) at Nagoji's stirrup, shouting up at him, face streaked with dust. Letter his balloon with a thin, wavering border: Nagoji hears him through ringing ears.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: The magazine! They hit the powder room!

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The church, Karl August had said. Stone walls keep damp out better than canvas.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Fire sweeping through the stockade on the wind, secondary explosions blooming along its length. Tiny distant figures running between burning huts. Keep them small and far.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought the explosion would break them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was wrong.

panels.description: Wide. Through smoke and flame, Dutch East India Company soldiers in blue coats and grey coats step out of the burning gaps in their wall. Not scattering: forming ranks, bayonets fixed, muskets levelled. Dhanaji's shout comes from the palm grove, off panel.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI (off)
copy.text: They're coming out!

panels.description: The first Dutch volley. A long bank of musket smoke along their line; our forward trench, men ducking and falling back from the parapet. Staging and distance only.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They fired and reloaded like men who had drilled until the motions lived in their bones.

panels.description: Our centre. Nair infantry (young, muscular, forward-tied topknots, bare chests, short white mundus, round shields) brace shields, swords and spears into a wall against the oncoming bayonets. At the centre of the line, set apart by age and build, Ramayyan: older, thin, receding hair, bare-headed, no shield, mud-splattered white dhoti, a curved Nair sword raised.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Hold!

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Hold the centre!

panels.description: The left flank, a grove of palms in deep shade. Nagoji on Kayal, the taller bay mare, among Maravar, Madurai and Deccan riders. Nagoji in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble. Dhanaji (white turban, indigo-dyed tunic) mounted at his shoulder. Ponnan beside them: bare-headed, curly hair uncovered, red shoulder cloth, white mundu hitched above bare knees, short jacket, on a smaller, lighter Maravar horse, a head lower than Nagoji. Nagoji leaning forward in the saddle, staring through the smoke.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They were not running to the sea. They were cutting their way out.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji's view from a slight rise at the palm line, looking down and across at the Dutch square through thinning smoke. Its front ranks are packed tight against the Nair line; its rear ranks are packed and facing the burning fort. Between them, the flank that faces the scrubland has thinned to a single ragged file with daylight showing through the gaps, and an officer's arm drags men out of that file toward the front.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: From the palms I saw what Ramayyan might have missed in the smoke.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The square had a seam.

panels.description: Nagoji drives Kayal out of the palms at a gallop, talwar drawn. Nagoji in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble. Behind him the Maravar, Madurai and Deccan riders burst from the grove in a single wave, Dhanaji's white turban among the first.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I did not wait for an order. I did not signal.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My riders followed like water through a broken dam.

panels.description: Rider's-eye view at speed, the horse's ears in the foreground. Dutch faces turning, eyes widening. A sergeant with his mouth open, arm out, trying to wheel his men. Bayonets catching sunlight at angles that will never meet a horse.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The last hundred yards stretched like hours.

panels.description: Wide. Impact. Our horse slams into the side of the square: horses rearing, steel flashing, men going down in dust and smoke. The ordered block of blue coats buckles.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A square that turns is no longer a square. It is a crowd.

panels.description: Inside the break, one instant. Dhanaji (white turban, indigo-dyed tunic) surges past Nagoji's shoulder into the gap, half a length ahead of him, sword raised; Deccan riders close behind. Beyond, in silhouette through the dust, a few Dutch soldiers fighting back to back.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Too close for their muskets. Too fast for their bayonets.

panels.description: Full width, bottom strip. Low and quiet. A Dutch musket drops into the trampled sand. Beyond it, out of focus, hands going up.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And then, as suddenly as it had begun, it was over.

panels.description: Wide. Sunset in lurid purples and reds through the smoke. The stockade burned down to glowing embers. The Dutch survivors huddled on the beach, some kneeling, some standing hollow-eyed with hands raised, their blue coats stained with ash.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They had not surrendered meekly.

panels.description: Through the haze, a tall, pale-haired man in a torn, soot-stained blue coat walks out from the Dutch lines toward ours, hands open at his sides. Behind him, Rijtel and two other surviving officers watch, hollow-eyed: shorter, dark-haired, officers' sashes, one with a bandaged arm.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He called to us in Portuguese.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: I am Eustachius De Lannoy. Captain of the Dutch East India Company.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: I speak for the garrison.

panels.description: Ramayyan steps forward to meet him, sword still in hand, dhoti splattered with mud and soot. In the background, a little apart, Varma mounted among his staff (varma-v1 face; cream-and-gold cloth, cream turban, gold necklaces), watching De Lannoy. No dialogue for the king.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You speak for men who burned our temples and took our people as slaves.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Why should we listen?

panels.description: De Lannoy, close. He does not flinch.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Because dead men cannot teach you how to build what we just lost.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: And I would rather build than rot.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji on Kayal some distance back from the parley, apart from the group, watching De Lannoy with narrowed eyes, the smoke of the ruined fort behind them both. Nagoji in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was the first time I heard those words from his own mouth. Later, I would learn what they meant.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In that moment, they sounded like a man who had already decided which side of the wall he wanted to stand on.

panels.description: Wide, twilight. Nagoji rides up to where Ramayyan stands. Nagoji in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no stubble. Ramayyan (older, thin, receding hair, bare-headed, mud-and-soot-splattered white dhoti) slides the curved Nair sword home into its sheath, the piece of silk he wiped it with still in his other hand, the motion as careful as calligraphy.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A general who cannot count is a butcher. Ramayyan could count, and he could kill.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They are done.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Yes. They are done.

panels.description: Ramayyan turns to look at the king. Varma (varma-v1 face; cream-and-gold cloth, cream turban, gold necklaces) on horseback, looking past them at the miserable huddle on the sand and, far out, the Dutch ships turning away in the deepening twilight. A Nair captain at his stirrup: young, forward-tied topknot, bare chest, short white mundu, round shield, no turban. Ramayyan in the foreground: bare-headed, receding hair, mud-and-soot-splattered white dhoti, no jewellery, sword sheathed.

copy.speaker: CAPTAIN
copy.text: Shall we finish them?

panels.description: Varma, close. Still, unhurried, the embers red on one side of his face.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: No.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Dead men cannot sign treaties. And they cannot teach us how to build what they just lost.

panels.description: Varma turning his horse away from the beach, speaking over his shoulder. Nagoji and Ramayyan watch him go.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Let them simmer tonight. Let them taste the ash.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Tomorrow, we will see what remains.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The smoking ruin of the fort under a last red sky. Prisoners walking in file along the beach, hands free or wrists bound in front, no ropes at the neck, guarded by Nair spearmen. Nagoji on Kayal in silhouette, small against it, the compact turban and the sash end readable in outline.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The explosion had wounded them. The cavalry had finished it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I knew the silence to come would be more dangerous than the noise. Now came the words.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: And words, in my experience, could be sharper than any sword.
